headline: Nvidia leadership vacuum collides with a fragile market rebound
body: Nvidia's abrupt leadership change is still the story markets are digesting: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president, and director effective November 11, with CFO Colette Kress stepping in as interim chief while the board searches for a permanent successor. Reporting ties the departure to a personal scandal rather than any disclosed business or accounting issue, and shares had already dropped sharply in the sessions before the announcement as news of the board's deliberations leaked. That shock landed on an already jittery tape — the broader market just finished clawing back part of an early-November, AI-valuation-driven selloff that had briefly driven a roughly 39% spike in the VIX and pushed the Nasdaq 100 about 10% off its October highs, with chipmakers including Micron, Intel, and AMD leading last week's bounce.

The combination leaves sentiment caught between relief and renewed caution rather than settled in either direction. A governance shock at the AI sector's bellwether, arriving just days before Nvidia's November 17 earnings, raises the stakes on that report considerably — it's now as much a test of whether an untested interim-CEO structure can hold investor confidence as it is a read on AI capital-spending demand. Fed December rate-cut odds remain unsettled in the background, with trader pricing and Fed commentary not fully aligned on timing. Today's retail and social-media chatter was too scattered across sources to read as a clear signal either way, so this take leans on price action, sector rotation, and the Nvidia headline rather than invented social-sentiment specifics.
